16	## Summary
17	
18	2D Lighting & Occlusion draws every light in the game: the player's chest-mounted beam, ship lamps, the glow of running machinery, the alarm beacon, glowsticks and fault glows, with real shadows from walls and a hull that is never fully black. It decides nothing about the world. It draws the facts Emitter State publishes, so the edge the player sees is the edge the game acts on (a prompt appears exactly where the light visibly ends), and it is the single place a light-shaped hallucination may be drawn, always as a violet-leaking overlay that never changes the real light beneath it. Skip it for what a light means (Emitter State) or where walls are (Layout).
19	
20	**Terms.** `reach_px` is the simulation's fade-out distance. `r_off` is the radius a soft pool is drawn to (the latch-release radius) and `r_lit` is the radius at which an approaching subject first meets its prompt, a few px inside it. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A slot is one of six shadow-casting lights. A layer is one step of the modifier chain. A stand-in is the additive disc, drawn to the same edge as the light it replaces, that stands in for an over-budget light. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A decoy is an unlit hallucination overlay, never a light. The tell tier is Attention's published level, drawn as a gutter on lamps.
21	
22	> **Quick reference** — Layer: Feature · Priority: MVP · Key deps: Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (designed), Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed in this run), Ship Section & Layout Data Model (designed); Attention, Horror Entities and Perception Filter are designed submitters
23	
24	## Overview
25	
26	**What it is, in one sentence.** 2D Lighting & Occlusion is the presentation-class renderer that turns the simulation's emitter records into the picture: every frame it reads the per-emitter view and the shape table that Emitter State publishes, and draws `Light2D` cones and pools, true occluder shadows, the ring and ship ambient, the material-level hull floor, the emission glow of running machinery and the light textures behind all of them, while owning no simulation fact of its own (no reach, no output, no `lit`, no block, no hook, nothing persisted).
27	
28	**Framing: a data/infrastructure layer with a very large player impact.** The player never meets "a lighting system". They meet a beam that ends hard at the exact place a prompt stops appearing, a wall that throws a shadow shaped like the wall, a lamp that sags when the ship is short of power, a machine glowing in its own colour in an otherwise black hull, and (late) a glow that runs past where their light really ends and leaks the wrong colour at its rim. The system is the *picture of the truth*: the simulation decides what is lit (Emitter State, `lit(ref)`, `illumination`); this GDD decides how that fact is drawn, and the two must agree to the pixel (hard cones at `reach_px` ±1 px, soft pools at the drawn radius `r_off` ±1 px, never smaller than where a prompt can live). The system exists for two reasons that pull in the same direction. First, **Pillar 1**: the physical radius your light actually reveals is one of the few anchors that never shift, and an anchor the player cannot see is not an anchor. Second, **Pillar 4**: a hallucination is frightening only against a picture that has been reliable for hours, and the single place where a light-shaped lie may be drawn is owned here, so that the lie can be bounded, made to leak, and never allowed to touch the real light beneath it. Without this system the game has no honest dark, no readable edge, no lanterns, no tell with a light channel, and no stage for the lie; and the art bible's first spike (the frame budget of six shadow-casting lights, many emissive loops and true occlusion on D3D12) stays unanswered, which the index names as the single decision on which the whole visual direction depends.
29	
30	**What it draws and what it owns.** Lighting is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber (kernel CR-10, KERN:108-113) with one `PROJECTOR`-class sub-duty (the occluder builder; treated as a `PROJECTOR` duty by default, default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), Open Question 5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. It reads last-committed `SIM` views and, for decoys and module-body glows only, `PERCEPTION_OUT` lists; it writes only `CanvasItem`, `Material`, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D` and `CanvasModulate` properties in layer 0 of the world viewport that the Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera GDD owns. It owns, by name: the light textures; per-shape light configuration conforming to the shape table; the six shadow-casting slots (`SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX`) and their assignment; the non-shadow light budget (`NONSHADOW_LIGHTS_MAX`, of which at most `LANTERN_LIGHTS_MAX` are node lanterns) and its deterministic demotion; occluder attachment over Layout's footprint rectangles (`OCCLUDER_POLYS_VIEW_MAX`, `OCCLUDER_VERTS_MAX`); ambient and the single shared HullSurface material with its floor; emission glow (the unshaded additive emissive layer and `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`); the warm-up, gutter and flicker recipes; the layered **modifier contract** through which Attention's tell, Horror's disturbance and the Perception Filter's decoys reach the picture without ever changing the real reveal radius; the per-light, regional and frame-mean flash governor (`flash_governor`, `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`); behaviour at every rung of the zoom ladder `k_z` in [1, `k_auto` + 2]; and the HR-15 low-vision raise and the reduce-flashing toggle as renderer-side consumers.
31	
32	**Index wording, reconciled.** The systems index (IDX:23, bullet 6, enumeration row 6, Recommended Design Order 9) says Lighting "owns the final Light2D values through a modifier contract: Attention flicker, horror light disturbance and Perception Filter decoys submit layered modifiers; the Filter may add decoy visuals but never changes the real reveal radius". This GDD keeps every clause and sharpens three words. "Final `Light2D` values" means every *value* member of every light (`enabled`, `energy`, `color`, `texture`, `texture_scale`, `offset`, shadow and range members); the local seat's beam *pose* members (`position`, `rotation`) are the Avatar Presenter's (Player Controller PC-5), so the two writers own disjoint member sets (LO-2). "Submit" means *publish state that Lighting reads* (KERN:117: "state that Lighting reads, not calls into Lighting"), never a call. "Attention flicker" is rendered as a **gutter** on fixtures (never the cryo-bay EMERGENCY lamp) and node lanterns only (the verb *flicker* is reserved for deployables, LO-30), an art-bible amendment this GDD requests rather than assumes. "Decoy visuals" are unlit overlays on a Lighting-owned layer and never lights (LO-21), which is what makes "never changes the real reveal radius" structural instead of a policy. The soft-cycle wording at IDX:266 ("Lighting never reads Attention") is superseded accordingly: Lighting reads Attention's published tell tier for the gutter recipe only and never derives reach, output, colour or edge from it.
33	
34	**What it is not.** It is not where light is *decided*: reach, output, `lit`, hysteresis, priority and the caps on emitters are Emitter State's; the Graph's `served_pm` is the only source of a lamp's brightness. It is not a builder: lights come with authored sections and welded modules, and the glowstick is the only player-placed light. It is not a combat system: a beam only reveals. It adds no meter, vignette, fog mask, gamma control or darkness penalty (LO-31). It does not own the viewport, the camera, `RENDER_MODE` or the z-bands (Pipeline), occluder geometry (Layout), hue tokens and hexes (art-director), or which decoy appears and when (Sanity and the Perception Filter).
35	
36	**MVP scope.** Single-player: one seat beam (slots, replication hints and the shape table are sized for four); the home ship and the two handmade derelicts (A with four compartments, B with five); the cryo-bay emergency lamp, which takes the sixth shadow slot; the three vacant beam-seat shadow slots, lent to the nearest wall-near static lights (LO-9, LO-33 mechanism C0) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; one alarm beacon; glowsticks; fault glows for the eight MVP faults that have a glow row; both render passes specified in full with pass A (lights at the 640x360 base resolution) the fallback and default until the lighting spike decides; the modifier contract with stubs for Attention (one tell tier) and Horror; and decoys as a contract plus a stub, because the MVP's single hallucination class (false system state) reaches light only through a lamp housing's own sprite (LO-14, LO-21). Flares, torches and decoy-deployables with their flicker, `GLOW_EXTENSION` and `PHANTOM_SHADOW` decoys, cross-body illumination and the three-ring ambient table are Vertical Slice A; four simultaneous beams and remote beam poses are Vertical Slice B.
37	
38	**Engine posture.** Godot 4.7.2, Forward+ pinned, D3D12 the Windows default since 4.6 (verified from `docs/engine-reference/godot/`, but the installed binary reports `vulkan` in the art bible's class dump, so the driver is written explicitly and printed at spike step 1). The reference folder has no `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D`, `CanvasModulate`, 2D-glow or `SubViewport` 2D-resolution content, and no `scripting.md` or `core.md` exists; every engine statement in this GDD therefore carries a tag, `[REF]` (verified from the reference), `[BIN]` (existence, type or default only, read from the installed 4.7.2 class dump recorded in the art bible 8.4 and 8.10) or `[UNV]` (unverified, settled by a named spike step), and costs the engine reference cannot source are marked NOT SOURCEABLE. The behaviour in this document is written so that a spike outcome selects between stated alternatives and never invalidates a rule.
39	
40	## Player Fantasy
41	
42	**Framing: indirect.** The player experiences this system as the picture itself (what is lit, what is dark, what changed) and never as "lighting". *(creative-director: Framing A "The Honest Dark" adopted as the headline with Framing B "Every Loop a Lantern" as its second beat; Framing C "Cinematic Dread Lighting", lights that flicker, swing and fail for mood and scripted blackouts, rejected because a light that changes without a cause the world can name breaks P1, a scare without a tell breaks P2, scripted events break the "no authored story" anti-pillar, and a liar outside the sanity system destroys the baseline Pillar 4 needs. Logged.)*
43	
44	> The dark here is not a fog. It is a ship with the lights off. The deck plates are there, a step above black, and anything you light shows exactly what it is. Where your beam ends, it ends hard, and a wall throws a shadow that is the shape of the wall.
45	>
46	> Every light you see has a reason. A lamp that sags is a ship short of power. A lamp that dips and comes back is something else, not the power. A machine glowing in its own colour is alive, and you are not the only one who can see it. A red sweep is the ship telling you it is losing. Nothing in the light moves for nothing.
47	>
48	> So you learn to read the ship by its lights, and the dark by its shadows. And when your mind starts to go, the picture is where the lie has to live: a glow that runs past where your light really ends, a shadow with nothing to cast it, a lamp that looks lit over a floor that is not. Every one of them is wrong at the edges, in a colour the sane ship never uses. Trust the floor, not the lamp.
49	
50	**The emotion named: the honest dark.** Trust in what you see, inside a place that frightens you. The horror of this game lives in instruments, sanity and the web; the light is the one thing the player learns to believe, and that trust is what makes Pillar 4 land (art bible Principle 1 rationale: "A hallucinated shadow with no occluder is then frightening *because* occlusion is normally trustworthy"). The power fantasy is **literacy, not dominance**: the player cannot push the dark back, but after an hour they can read a ship from its lights the way a sailor reads a harbour at night: which lamps are sagging (power), which one dipped (something noticed), which machines are lanterns (alive and seen), and whose shadow that is (a real wall, or not). In MDA terms the system serves Discovery (the picture is how a derelict is read) and Challenge (lamp sag and fault glow are diagnostic), and is the main carrier of Sensation (CON:87, "HD pixel art under a light-as-resource rendering model; flow-coded loops glowing in the dark"); it must never buy Sensation at the cost of the first two.
51	
52	**Division of labour with Emitter State's fantasy.** Emitter State owns "the bargain of sight": where the edge is, that the edge equals the prompt, light as a spend, exposure, the reach-for-it falsifier and the per-kind meaning table (EM Player Fantasy). This section does not repeat it. Lighting's fantasy is the **picture**: that the dark is *drawn* honestly (geometry present, hull above black), that every change in a light's look has a cause in the world, the grammar of a dimming lamp, the ship as lanterns, shadow as testimony, how the picture holds at every zoom rung, and where a lie is allowed to live in the picture and how it leaks.
53	
54	**Anchor moment: the cryo-bay wake (the first minute of the game).** You wake. One emergency lamp hangs low and dim in Tungsten (ART 2.2; fixture hex `#FFCC66`), and it **gutters**: a dip of 0.3-0.5 s, then another 10-20 s later, never on a beat. It holds the sixth shadow slot (LO-9), so the pod row throws short, hard shadows down-screen: the room has walls you can trust before you have touched anything. The far wall is suggestion only, an ambient near 3 % over a hull floor that never drops to true black (`HULL_FLOOR_TINT` `#0B1018`, `HULL_FLOOR_GAP_STEPS`). If the pod you came out of carries a light, it is a real FIXTURE placement whose `output_pm` falls in the simulation, never a Lighting-only effect (a Lighting-only glow would be a light that exposes nothing, a P1/P3 lie); Derelict Authoring has answered "no cryo-pod light in the MVP" (DA-23), and any later pod light is a real FIXTURE placement (Ask E-H). You switch on the chest lamp: the light lands on the committed tick and warms over at most `LAMP_WARM_FRAMES` without its edge ever moving. A frost trail crosses the floor in Coolant Ice and catches in your cone. The lesson of minute one: **the lamp you did not choose is a fact; the light you did choose is a decision; neither one lies.** The cryo lamp is also the one fixture the Attention tell never touches (LO-20), so nothing the player sees in this room can be the web leaning in: the gutter here is the room's baseline and the first tell arrives later, on a home-ship lamp, read against it. *What the player must not be able to confuse here:* the gutter (a dip, the lamp's readable radius keeps its size) with a real light going out (simulation state, for example a pod light if the placement carries one).
55	
56	**Second beat: the home ship, conserved (Framing B).** Before a sortie you kill the corridor lamps. Home-ship ambient falls from about 10 % (stable) toward about 2 % (dark) (ART 4.3, `AMBIENT_HOME_STABLE_PM` / `AMBIENT_HOME_DARK_PM`), not because a menu said so but because the fixtures that set it went out. What is left is the scrubber, glowing O2 Cyan `#3FD6E8` along its pipe (an emissive overlay) and casting light at its node (a node lantern), and the reactor cell in Power Amber `#F2C230`: "isolated lanterns in a black hull" (ART 2.4). You can count them. So can the web. The image is the creative core of this system: **the ship drawn only by what you keep alive.**
57	
58	**Third beat: the tell (P2 and P3 in one lamp).** Back on the home ship with lamps on, the scrubber pulls power and the galley lamp **sags**: steadily, and its pool *pulls in* (a fixture served at 600 permille is drawn at 60 % energy with its pool ending at 115 px instead of 126 px, `r_off` 115 px by the integer chain of D.3, while a subject walking in meets its prompt at `r_lit` 108 px, the published `r_lit_px`, `EM D.7`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The junction box at the old edge loses its prompt. A minute later the same lamp **dips**: 0.3-0.5 s at no less than `MOD_FLOOR_PM` of its served brightness, and its readable pool does **not** shrink (no modifier touches the texture radius, LO-18; on a dark floor the soft rim may look a little closer for the length of the dip, which is why the dependable cue is that it returns, Named rule 1). Then again, sooner. Your beam does not change at all (the beam is "a truth anchor", ART 2.7). That is Attention's tell tier, the web leaning in, and the only light-side tell in the MVP's one Attention tier. The player who has learned the grammar knows the second event is not the power.
59

157	### Core Rules

161	**LO-1. Rendering only; Lighting reads, the simulation never reads Lighting.** Lighting is a `PRESENTATION` subscriber (KERN:108-113). It reads the last-committed `SIM` views (`emitter.state` and its `shapes()` table, Layout's `OccluderSource`) and, for decoys and module-body glows only, `PERCEPTION_OUT` lists; its notification handlers only mark dirty (kernel CR-10: handler = dirty mark only, writes disabled in handlers) and all drawing happens in the render callback. It writes only `CanvasItem`, `Material`, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D` and `CanvasModulate` properties, all inside layer 0 of the world viewport that the Pipeline owns. It owns no simulation fact, no reach, no output, no `lit`; it never writes an emitter, never reports a cull to the simulation (a sim-lit but unrendered light would be a P1 lie, so the answer to over-budget is demotion, LO-23, not silence), and registers **no state block, no step hook and no `after:` entry**. Hook ids appear in this document only as things Lighting does *not* order against (`emitter.place`, `body.integrate`) and never in an example. The occluder builder (LO-11) is the one derived-object duty and is classed `PROJECTOR` (KERN:112); the kernel marks that reading provisional pending a technical-director ruling (KERN:117, Open Question 1) and this GDD does not pre-empt it (-> ADR candidate: occluder projector class). The test for ownership (mirroring Emitter State guard G1): if a sentence needs a `Light2D` to be true it belongs here, otherwise it belongs to the owner and is cited by name.

167	**LO-4. Clocks, and what a "frame" means in a knob.** Three clocks, each with one job. The **kernel clock** (`tick` and `tick_alpha`) drives everything the simulation also computes and that `lit` depends on: the beacon's aim, beam and deployable poses, a glowstick's wane. `present_time` (Pipeline PR-9; frozen while `PAUSED`) drives purely cosmetic phase and duration: gutter dips, flare micro-flicker, fringe breathing, warm-up and fade envelopes, the governor's rolling window. The tick counter is never used for anything animated (PIPE PR-8 rule 6) and wall-clock is never used. **The `*_FRAMES` knobs have two units, stated once here, because LO-3 runs two cadences.** The per-render-frame envelopes (`LAMP_WARM_FRAMES`, `SHADOW_FADE_FRAMES`, `CUT_FADE_FRAMES`, `AMBIENT_SLEW_FRAMES`) count **1/`TICK_RATE` of a second of `present_time`** (one frame = 16.67 ms at `TICK_RATE` 60), independent of the render rate, so `LAMP_WARM_FRAMES` 5 is 83.3 ms at 30, 60 or 144 fps. The per-committed-tick decisions (`SLOT_DWELL_FRAMES`, which LO-9 counts in consecutive ticks, `CUT_HYSTERESIS_FRAMES`, `FULL_RECONCILE_TICKS`) count **committed ticks**, observed at the per-tick cadence. The two units are equal whenever the kernel keeps up and diverge only under simulation lag (kernel CR-17), when a decision is slower in wall time but never reordered. Every other time quantity in this GDD is written in seconds or in the unit of its own clock (the Tuning Knobs table carries a Unit column); the names are those of the ruling. While the kernel is `PAUSED`, envelopes, gutters, the governor window and flare phase freeze and the beacon's drawn aim holds because the kernel clock holds. **The beacon's drawn aim is the kernel clock's `beacon_aim(T)` interpolated with `tick_alpha`, not `present_time`**: the drawn cone must equal the cone `lit` uses (P1), and `present_time` and the kernel clock diverge under simulation lag (kernel CR-17) and after a restore. PIPE PR-9 lists "the beacon's sweep phase" among `present_time`'s consumers; that is a refresh owed (Cross-References), and only the beacon's non-geometric cosmetic phase (if any) stays on `present_time`.

304	**LO-25. Truth channel and corruptible channel; the isolation lint.** No real light reads `PERCEPTION_OUT` for `enabled`, `energy`, `color`, `texture_scale`, `offset` or pose. Source lints assert: (i) the Presenter's `Light2D` writes are exactly `position` and `rotation` (LO-2); (ii) the Filter writes no `Light2D` member and the kernel's row-11 sentence "Filter writes only CanvasItem/Material/Light2D" is stale (a refresh owed); (iii) Lighting's `PERCEPTION_OUT` reads are confined to the decoy list and the module-body glow channel; (iv) `emitter.state` has no field named `phantom`, `perceived`, `decoy` or `hallucinated` (EM-29); (v) no tool-layer node carries a light; (vi) no verb, hue or token outside LO-8 and LO-30 appears. Hidden real entities do not cast "a shadow with no occluder"; that is the stage-2 sanity tell and must stay unambiguous. Lighting never tints a real light, so if the Perception Filter's full-screen container pass (PIPE PR-10) delivers the stage-2 "apparent temperature drifts warm" (ART 2.9) over beam pixels it recolours the human channel, a Filter-side defect: the Filter must deliver warm drift on non-anchor content only or mask beam pixels (CONFLICT CD-2, routed to the art-director and the Perception Filter; -> ADR candidate: container-pass truth mask).
305	
306	**LO-26. Accessibility: reduce-flashing and HR-15 (both per client).** *Reduce flashing* (a toggle separate from reduced motion, PIPE PR-13 (c)): deployables become steady (flicker and dips replaced by steady energy), power arcs become a held glow at their mean luminance, the beacon **keeps its sweep** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* (one sweep per 2.13 s is about 0.47 per second against the limit of 3, so a static mark would buy no measured safety and would remove the P2 "the ship is losing" image; the governor applies to the sweep exactly as it does with the setting off; there is no HUD glyph under any setting: a breach glyph would be an Attention indicator, ART:741, Attention C27), the cryo gutter is kept (a rare presence cue that passes the clamp), and the Attention gutter is kept at its spacing (it passes by construction); toggling it mid-dip snaps the **deployable flicker's** `M1` to full on the next frame as a single transition that the governor counts normally (the EMERGENCY lamp's `M1` gutter shares the layer name but is not touched, which is why the gutter is "kept"). **Scope, stated once:** the setting reduces only the effects that approach the limit (deployable flicker and dips, power arcs, the flare flicker); if a later measurement shows the sweep itself is a hazard, its reduced form is defined geometrically (a low-contrast cone that still follows `beacon_aim(T)`), never a static mark. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* *HR-15 low-vision raise:* a per-client raise of the HullSurface floor by 0 to `HR15_STEP_MAX` (3) steps above the measured floor (proposal: one 8-bit code per step), **hull geometry only**, never web, horrors, filaments, lights or the HUD; changing it changes nothing but the floor term and `ambient_pm`, applied at the next apply step. There is no full-frame gamma or brightness anywhere, and the root viewport never carries `CanvasModulate` or gamma (PIPE PR-3). The first-launch "barely visible" reference swatch is drawn with the real floor values and writes no game value (PIPE Open Question 5); Settings owns the UI. **Config defaults (design review):** `reduce_flashing` defaults to **ON at first launch** (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D79 / X10; the player may turn it off in Display & Comfort) and the HR-15 step to **0**, both per client and host-local, read through the Settings store interface (the Chart Table & Menus page holds the toggle and the first-launch notice tells the player it is on and offers turning it off; the HR-15 step has no page at the MVP and stays 0 until Settings & Input Rebinding, Pipeline PR-14), and neither is ever read by the simulation. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
307	
308	**LO-27. Per-kind specifics: the beacon, the glowstick, the fault glow.** *The beacon* is a 20-degree-half-angle HARD cone (shape row 8) whose axis is the pure function of the kernel clock `beacon_aim(T)` (`BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 = 2.13 s), interpolated with `tick_alpha` and wrap-aware (LO-4), so **the drawn cone leads the committed cone by at most 32 units (2.8 degrees) inside a tick, the same divergence class PC-5 accepts for the beam; `lit` is evaluated against the committed cone only**; it occupies slot 5; a fixed point is covered 14-15 of every 128 ticks; its Alarm Red appears on no other light; `gates_actions` is false (EM-16); the governor counts its sweep (about 0.47 flashes per second for a fixed observer, ESTIMATE) and never delays its rotation; after a restore the aim jumps to the restored `T` under the hold quad. Under the red sweep, lit albedo takes the red channel almost alone, so hue fidelity is a spike item (step 8) and greyscale polarity and form carry the read (FT row 8). *The glowstick* appears from its **landing tick** only (Interaction's `throw_glowstick`, landing at T + `THROW_ARC_TICKS`; Lighting never pre-plays a throw, PC:989); it is steady, then wanes in integer `reach_px` steps (`GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM`, `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM`, `EM D.9`: simulation state, never a presentation effect), and each integer step redraws the pool at the new `r_draw` on the committed tick with no tween and no flicker; waning **changes the real reveal radius**, so it changes the drawn radius, which is the P1 point; at most `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` (4) stack, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` (8) live, and an evicting stick wanes over `GLOWSTICK_EVICT_WANE_S`. *The fault glow* appears on the Graph tick of its descriptor with the radius and hue of its Failure & Trail row (rows `1/FUEL`, `1/GAS`, `2`, `3`, `7`, `9`; the default radius is `FAULT_GLOW_REACH_PX`), is exempt from L2 and L3, and is never demoted while younger than 600 ticks.
309	
310	**LO-28. Local and remote beams; the chest lamp.** The lamp is chest-mounted and hands-free: the beam is available in every state the player can act in and is on while carrying or channelling, and the tool layer carries no light (the hand point is lightless; only lit-only channelled verbs consult `lit(ref)`). The beam's origin is the per-facing chest point (`|x| ≤ 2`); the local seat's pose is the Presenter's (LO-2); the beam's shape and colour come from the loadout and are never modified (the identity channel). The MVP beam has constant output (no charge dimming: Suit's stage ruling, provisional; Suit never sets `output_pm`), but `output_pm` below 1000 on a beam is supported generically: drawn dimmer, its HARD rim below `LIT_ON_PM` under 600 permille (LO-6). **Remote beams (VS-B)** have no Presenter: Lighting interpolates the replicated record pair with `tick_alpha` and a wrap-aware angle, floors the origin to base px in the body frame (PIPE PR-4 rules 2 and 8, one interpolator), and never rewrites shape or colour; no modifier, decoy or LOD touches a beam's colour, shape or reach. A DOWNED seat's beam stays lit, draining, and stays a locator at its last committed aim while that crewmate cannot act; `force_off` comes only at zero charge or at DEAD, where the Emitter State forces it off (Suit SE-24); the held aim is assumed pending the Controller (Open Question 14).
311	
312	**LO-29. Persistence, restore and holds.** Lighting persists **nothing** and registers no block, no step hook and no `after:` entry; the Save/Load GDD does not name Lighting, and its provisional block inventory (SL-25) lists Failure & Trail as "None, pure reader and renderer"; an ask to add an equivalent Lighting row is in Cross-References. After a restore Lighting re-derives every light and occluder from `emitter.state` and the Layout `version` counter once the kernel has finished sequencing blocks (CR-8 `post_restore`), discards every governor window, dwell timer, gutter epoch, last-written cache and binding, and treats the first full reconcile as a first observation (LO-3). **Restore equality (design review):** after a restore the picture equals the pre-save picture in *lit emitters, positions, radii and L0 energy* (the tick-only decisions of LO-3); envelopes, gutter phases, shadow fades and the governor history restart (a lamp that was mid-dip returns to full), so the equality is of those quantities and not of every modulated pixel. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* During `LOADING` and `TRANSIT_HOLD` the world is under the hold quad (PIPE :99) and lights are not updated (the world viewport may render underneath the hold quad for material warm-up: HullSurface, Emissive and Fringe are each drawn once for every variant of the **warm-up variant matrix** (shaders {HullSurface, Emissive, Fringe, the stand-in additive, the decoy mix, the Filter's default-off include block} × lights bound {none, one non-shadow, one shadow-casting, the engine's overlap cap on one item} × pass {A, B} × `hdr_2d` on) so no shader variant compiles on first use in play *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; whether the Shader Baker `[REF]` covers canvas shaders is `[UNV]`, step 10). The MVP's death handling is restart from the last autosave (Save/Load): Lighting takes no further position than "nothing to restore".
313	
314	**LO-30. The verb vocabulary is fixed and lintable (ruled R27).** Arcs *pop*; deployables *flicker*; the cryo lamp *gutters* and, at the Attention tell, so do fixtures and node lanterns; pipes *glow*; fuel edges *glint*; glowsticks *wane* (simulation state, never a presentation effect); the beacon *sweeps*. "Flicker" never describes a fixture, lantern, beacon, beam or glowstick. The stale-token scan greps each verb against its allowed subjects.

316	**LO-31. No meter, no darkness cost.** There is no light meter, exposure ring, brightness readout, world-space light marker, vignette, fog mask, darkness debuff effect, gamma or brightness slider (P3 "never a meter"; PIPE PR-13 (d)). Darkness is never a sanity cost or a rendered penalty (EM Open Question 4); go-dark is a valid, unpenalised strategy and must be legible as light (the ship's lit area falls to what runs). The gameplay surfaces of this system are the lit picture and what it gates by proxy: prompts are the HUD's, gated by `lit(ref)` from Emitter State, never by the renderer (PIPE :104 (d)); the HUD, hold quad, menus and debug are other viewports or CanvasLayers and are unlit by construction. Debug Overlay surfaces (`DIAGNOSTIC`, dev builds only, absent from release): occluder outlines (`draw_line` width at least 1 base px, no AA feather `[REF]`), slot assignment, the modifier stack per light, the governor log, `r_lit` circles, the LOD tier and the `diag.*` counters.
317	
318	**LO-32. Spike-gated decisions: which step decides what.** The ten-step plan is ART 8.12 (PIPE proposes steps 11-13: stretch and window, motion integrity, pacing). Lighting does not own `RENDER_MODE`; it participates in step 2 and must work under either result. "Confirmed by the spike" means confirmed or **revised with a logged conflict**, never restated silently. Step 3 confirms the containment mechanism that ships (C0, the lent slots, inside the six-shadow composition) and step 4 decides whether the C1 fallback of LO-33 is viable. **Spike precondition (design review).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Steps 1-4, 7a and the new filter probe 2c are a **precondition for `/create-epics`**, delivered as a Sprint-0 story with retained captures in `production/qa/evidence/`, together with the full-cap composition per LOD tier (every cap filled, the lent slots, beams and beacon) and its GPU ms, draw-call and VRAM readings against the RenderingServer counters `[UNV]` (the reference machines RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK are named, R12; the Lighting GPU sub-budget is set from these measurements at the spike, and the Pipeline GDD excludes Lighting's cost: Open Question 28) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*. **Locked contracts versus revisable placeholders:** the locked contracts are the ±1 px hard edge, the ±1 px prompt agreement of LO-7 in both directions of approach, `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 and the hull never fully black; a spike result that fails a locked contract is a **failure** and changes the design, and only a placeholder number (an energy, a margin, a count) may be revised with a logged conflict. **Owner of the 2D renderer environment:** the world-viewport glow `Environment` and `SubViewport.use_hdr_2d` belong to the Pipeline (it owns the viewport), are read back by its PR-15 startup assertion, and Lighting states what it needs (hdr_2d on, glow on at `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`, debanding, **and the `Environment` carrying a Canvas background mode, which debanding and 2D glow need `[UNV]` and which the Pipeline did not list** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*).
319	
320	**LO-33. Containment: a non-shadow light draws only where the simulation's segment can reach (CD-GDD-ALIGN revision; named P1 divergence PD-1; the shipping mechanism is named by the design review of 2026-10-27; owners technical-artist and engine-programmer).**
321	
322	*The gap this rule closes.* Emitter State occludes every emitter in the simulation (EM-20: the closed, conservative segment test over Layout's `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` occupied spans, covering its static layer of FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN, FAULT_GLOW and resting DEPLOYABLE as well as the dynamic BEAM and BEACON; it fails safe to dark). In the render only the six shadow-slot lights (LO-9) are checked against `LightOccluder2D`. Every other real light is a non-shadow `PointLight2D` that lights every item whose mask intersects its own inside its quad, so in the MVP only the beam, the beacon and the cryo lamp stop at a bulkhead on screen. A full fixture draws a pool of `r_draw` up to 126 px (2.6 tiles); behind a one-cell wall (24 px) that pool can reach up to 126 − 24 = 102 px into the next compartment (arithmetic, worst case with the fixture touching its own wall face). Without this rule the sane picture lights a room the simulation calls dark, with no violet leak: a P1 lie, free information about neighbouring rooms, and a break of "go dark is legible as light" (P3) when a neighbour's pool spills into a conserved room. LO-7 (sim-lit skirts the render shows dark) and LO-23 (sim-lit lights left unrendered) cover the opposite direction, and the radius lints cover radius only.
323	
324	*The invariant (I-CONTAIN), narrowed by the design review.* For every real light `L` and every lit item or registered subject `s` in view: if the simulation's segment test (EM-20) says the segment from `L`'s origin to `s` is blocked **by an inter-compartment wall or door leaf** (an `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangle that bounds two compartments), then `L`'s drawn light does not contribute to `s`'s pixels. Shadow-slot lights (including the three lent slots, LO-9) meet it through their occluders (LO-11); every other real light (FIXTURE not EMERGENCY, NODE_LANTERN, FAULT_GLOW, a glowstick not holding a slot, and demoted stand-ins) meets it through the bounded mechanism below. **The prop-occluder leak is outside I-CONTAIN and is its own named divergence, PD-1b:** a tall prop or machinery body flagged `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` shadows the simulation's segment *inside* one compartment (a NODE_LANTERN sits beside exactly such a body at a machinery node), but a non-shadow pool is drawn over the floor behind it under every candidate mechanism, so a sim-dark subject in a prop's lee can stand inside a drawn pool; PD-1b has its own numeric bound below. **Containment errs toward the dark** wherever it cannot be exact: a missing sliver of pool is bounded and still shown by the housing and the consequence channel, while a pool through a wall leaks information the player has no way to falsify (P4: no lie unfalsifiable). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
325	
326	*The decision (design review): C0 plus a bounded C3 ships in the MVP; C1 is the named fallback.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The earlier preference for C1 is withdrawn for the MVP. godot-specialist found that `light_mask` is a per-`CanvasItem` property and a `TileMapLayer` has no per-tile mask `[BIN]`, so C1 cannot be built on one tilemap layer per section: it needs one render node per body × compartment × z-band, which is a Layout (ADR-LAY-03) and Pipeline decision on node count and draw cost, plus an unverified 20-bit any-shared-bit rule and a compartment-of-cell answer (Ask E-J) for which Layout has no row. A result at spike step 3 or 4 that moves a value is a logged conflict (LO-32).
327	
328	- **C0 (ships in the single-player MVP): lend the vacant beam-seat shadow slots (LO-9).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Seats 2-4 are vacant in the single-player MVP, so the three nearest wall-near non-shadow-kind lights to the local seat (four while no BEACON is loaded and `LEND_BEACON_SLOT` is on, LO-9; the predicate and the ranking, with its hysteresis, are LO-9's) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* are given a slot and cast real `LightOccluder2D` shadows: their pools stop at every bulkhead, stop at a door leaf and pass through an open door's aperture exactly as the simulation's segment does, with no new mask bits (`CONTAIN_COLOURS` 1), no change to Layout and the engine's own shadow code. The composition is the one spike step 3 already measures (six shadow-casting lights), the honest picture holds in the rooms where the player actually stands, and because a tall prop is also an `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangle the wall-near predicate puts a light beside a prop into the lent set, which closes PD-1b for the nearest three. **Named fallback if C0 fails** (step 3 shows the six-shadow composition over budget at the largest ladder field, or VS-B binds a remote seat and the lent light reverts to a non-shadow pool): C1 below.
329	- **C1 (named fallback; required for VS-B): compartment-colour mask bits.** Extends the pattern of LO-24 (partition bits, any-shared-bit semantics `[UNV]`). `bit(body_index, colour)` is defined in LO-24; `CONTAIN_COLOURS` is a placeholder of 4 (range 1-6; 1 means containment off, one bit per body). The authoring lint colours each body's compartment adjacency graph greedily so that **no two compartments whose floor regions lie within `R_DRAW_MAX_PX + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` of each other share a colour**, where `R_DRAW_MAX_PX` is the largest `r_draw` at 1000 permille among non-shadow kinds in the shape table (126 px, FIXTURE R 144, for the MVP; it was 122 px when the pool was drawn to `r_lit`, a refresh owed to Derelict Authoring) and `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` is 24 px (EM-20). The MVP bodies hold 5, 4 and 5 compartments, so at most 5 colours are ever needed, and the lint reports the number it needed (Derelict Authoring's authored layouts need 3, within `CONTAIN_COLOURS` 4: DA C-9); a body that needs more than `CONTAIN_COLOURS` fails authoring. **Build constraint (godot-specialist):** `light_mask` is per `CanvasItem` and a `TileMapLayer` has no per-tile mask `[BIN]`, so C1 means **one render node per body × compartment × z-band** (floor 0, marks +1, Y-sort +10), whose count and draw cost need Layout (ADR-LAY-03) and Pipeline sign-off before it is chosen; Ask E-J supplies the compartment-of-cell answer; it is not built unless C0 fails or VS-B arrives. **Items:** floor and prop chunks are compartment-aligned (a chunk never spans two compartments, so the chunk of LO-23 splits at a wall line; the ADR value `ITEM_CHUNK_TILES` stays a maximum, not a fixed square); a wall cell, a door-aperture cell and a character footprint carry the colour of every compartment they overlap. **Lights:** a non-shadow light carries exactly one bit, its own compartment's colour for its body; a shadow-slot light carries every colour bit of its body, because its containment is its occluder set and an open doorway must pass its light exactly as the simulation's segment does. A slot-6 swap switches the light's bit set in the same apply step as the slot state, and spike step 3b verifies that no frame shows either a pop or a leak. **Bit budget:** `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` × `CONTAIN_COLOURS` = 4 × 4 = 16 bits at indices 4 to 19, which fits a mask of 20 bits `[UNV]` with bit 20 spare; if step 4 finds fewer than 20, `CONTAIN_COLOURS` falls first (its range floor is 1) and the lint reports the colours the MVP needs, so the cost is known before a bit is spent.
330	- **C2: per-compartment canvas layers** with `range_layer_min` / `range_layer_max` `[UNV]`, LO-24's existing second choice; **rejected for the MVP**: lighting across canvases is `[UNV]` and the layers split the Pipeline's single Y-sorted layer 0, so it is taken only if C1's bits do not fit.
331	- **C3 bounded (ships beside C0, for every light C0 does not lend a slot to): the authoring lint, defined per wall face by room depth (Derelict Authoring C-9 / OQ-DA-28).** For each non-shadow light and each `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` wall run whose far side is lit floor of **another compartment** (a hull wall onto void or exterior is exempt), the spill depth is `s = max(0, r_draw − d_face − WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`, where `d_face` is the distance from the light's origin to that wall's near face along the wall normal and `r_draw` is taken at 1000 permille (the largest `r_draw`, 126 px for the fixture), or at the placement's actual `r_draw` for a lamp that is never at full output. A placement passes when `s` is 0 on every such face, i.e. when its origin sits at least `r_draw` − 24 px (102 px for a full 144 px FIXTURE) from each interior face that backs onto another compartment; the lint never demands a room of any width. **The earlier reading is withdrawn:** a 244 px clear span in both axes (2 × the then-current 122 px) treated every wall as backing onto a neighbour and, read literally, failed 12 of the 14 authored rooms (DA C-9, PD-1), against ART 6.4 and PIPE:874. A room whose depth between two interior faces is under 2 × (`r_draw` − 24) cannot pass on both faces with a full fixture; there the lamp is moved toward its hull side or kept and logged as a PD-1 exception with its spill depth `s` (residual bound (i) below), and the room is never resized for the lint. C3 is **the shipping mitigation for every light C0 does not lend a slot to, bounded numerically in the residual bounds below; it is not sufficient alone.**
332	- **Not available:** raising `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` (6, locked; raising it is a CONFLICT to surface and is not made here).
333	
334	*Open doors.* Under C0 an open door needs no rule of its own: the leaf rectangle is the occluder (LO-11) and the lent light's pool passes through the aperture exactly as the simulation's segment does. **The rest of this paragraph is the C1 fallback.** While a door is open (`leaf_w` < `width_px`, LY-9) the simulation's segment passes through the gap. Under C1 the door cells themselves (the cells the leaf occupies in the wall line) carry both neighbours' colours like any wall cell, and the one-cell **far-side strip** is its own item whose `light_mask` gains the near side's colour **only while `leaf_w` < `width_px`**, applied in the same apply step as the occluder swap of LO-11, so it follows the committed leaf with at most one tick of lag (the same acceptance as LO-11's door text); while the door is closed the strip carries its own colour only and a closed door leaks nothing. The rest of the through-gap light on the far side is drawn dark. **Named step-4 sub-case, wall-face directionality:** a wall cell lit from a north room shows its lit face to a viewer standing south of it, so the bulkhead can read as lit from the south side; the spike measures whether the wall cell must carry directional (north-face and south-face) items rather than both colours on one item, and until it does the wall-cell lit face is accepted as a bounded sub-case counted by `diag.contain_leak`. That is the sim-lit, render-dark class of LO-7 (a prompt may be actionable in a corridor that looks unlit past the strip), accepted as the lesser lie by the dark-erring rule above, bounded by `diag.contain_dark` (count of in-view subjects that are sim-lit and outside every drawn pool) and measured at step 4. A wider strip (`DOOR_SPILL_CELLS`, proposed 1, range 1-3) re-admits render-lit and sim-dark where the through-gap geometry bends behind a corner, and is taken only if a capture shows the dark sliver is unreadable.
335	
336	*Stand-ins.* A demoted light's emissive stand-in (LO-23) is **drawn to `r_draw` on every azimuth, with no isotropic or directional wall clamp and no minimum size**, so it ends where the bound light's pool would have ended and where its prompt ends (LO-7, AC-LO-73). Its spill across an `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` wall is the same spill the bound, unlent pool would have had, and it is counted under the same residual bounds: bound (i) for an authored static light (the C3 lint is evaluated at the light's `r_draw`, so a lantern that passes the lint as a pool passes it as a stand-in), bound (ii) for a glowstick, and `diag.contain_leak` for every in-view stand-in disc whose `r_draw` crosses an `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangle onto lit floor of another compartment. A wall-mounted fixture, which LO-33 models as touching its own wall face, is therefore drawn in full (the mounting wall is never measured). **The earlier isotropic clamp is withdrawn** (it clamped a stand-in to the nearest `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` edge, drew nothing below 4 px, and made a wall-mounted lantern's stand-in vanish while its pool had been 126 px wide): it contradicted LO-17, LO-23, AC-LO-38/40/60/73 and the zoom-out promise that counting lanterns at `k_z` 1 and walking up to read a prompt agree to 1 base px. The cost it protected was already accepted in bounds (i) to (iv). If a clamp is ever reintroduced it must measure only far-side inter-compartment walls (never the mounting wall), be directional, and clamp up to 4 px rather than omit, and the zoom-out promise must then be struck everywhere and the lantern-count cost put to the user. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
337	
338	*Residual bounds under C0 plus C3: PD-1 narrowed, and PD-1b (a scoped MVP exception with a numeric bound, an owner and a closing trigger).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (i) **Static lights.** Every authored FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN and FAULT_GLOW placement in the three MVP bodies passes the C3 lint at spill depth `s` = 0, or is moved, or is kept with `s` at most `PD1_EXCEPTION_MAX_PX` (24 px, one wall cell: the user's number, ruling D31, not a placeholder) and logged as a PD-1 exception with its spill depth; a placement above 24 px fails authoring, and authoring may not rely on a lent slot because the lend follows the seat. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R7 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): the bound stays 24 px and AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING; no exception list is added for shipped content.** The home ship's `spine_corridor` (144 px between its two interior faces, so `d_face` is 72 px at the centre line, the most any placement can give) is recomputed at the registry's `R_DRAW_MAX_PX` 126: `s` = 126 − 72 − 24 = **30 px**, not Derelict Authoring's 26 px (computed at the stale 122), so it fails the lint as authored and Derelict Authoring must bring it within 24 by the least invasive change (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing; the room is never resized for the lint). 491	## Formulas
492	
493	Nineteen formulas, numbered `D.1`-`D.19` in the order of the list that closes Core Rules (LO-32); Core Rules keeps citing them by registry name. Every formula that is not this GDD's is qualified (`EM D.7`, `PIPE D.5`, `kernel D.10`) and is reused by name, never restated with another value. **Integer discipline:** Lighting persists and replicates nothing (LO-29), so floats appear only where a value is handed to the engine in the apply step (`energy`, `texture_scale`, `offset`); every *decision* quantity (counts, ranks, the permille chain, the governor window, hashes, tier boundaries) is an integer, and every decision is a pure function of the committed read view, the committed camera field, the present clock, the per-client settings and the previous decision (LO-3). Every number introduced here is a placeholder, owner technical-artist, "confirmed by the Lighting spike step n"; every `ESTIMATE` is arithmetic on a stated model, not a measurement. Pixel and texel counts are in base px unless a column says screen px.
494	
495	### D.1 Light energy from output
496	
497	The `light_energy_from_pm` formula is defined as:
498	
499	`E_L0 = LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM × KIND_GAIN[kind] × output_pm`
500	
501	**Variables:**
502	
503	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
504	|---|---|---|---|---|
505	| `output_pm` | int | 0..1000 | `emitter.state` read view (SIM) | served brightness; the only source of a real light's brightness (LO-8) |
506	| `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM` | float | 0.0005..0.0015; placeholder 0.001 | ★ owner technical-artist; spike steps 2, 7, 8 | engine energy per permille; `E_1000` = `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM` × 1000 |
507	| `KIND_GAIN[kind]` | float | 0.6..1.4; placeholder 1.0 each | Tuning Knobs | per-kind trim so fixtures can sit under beams without touching the shared constant |
508	| `E_L0` | float | 0.30..2.10 at full output (0.0005..0.0015 × 0.6..1.4 × 1000); 0 when `output_pm` is 0 | output | layer-0 energy, the ceiling of every later layer |
509	
510	**Output Range:** 0 to `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM` × `KIND_GAIN` × 1000 (1.000 at the defaults); non-decreasing in `output_pm`, so **a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served** (`EM D.1`, Graph D.6). Two bounds on `E_1000`: below, the rim must stay legible on mid Graphite, `E_1000` ≥ lin(floor code + `RIM_VIS_CODES`) / (`EDGE_FLOOR_PM` / 1000 × A_G × c_G) with floor code 1, `RIM_VIS_CODES` 8, A_G 0.0296 (Graphite mid green, linear) and c_G 0.761 (beam green) = 0.00273 / 0.00562 = 0.49 (ESTIMATE); above, the bloom bound of D.8, which includes `KIND_GAIN` and `N_OVERLAP_MAX` and is asserted at startup. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Example:** a fixture at 1000 permille draws 0.001 × 1.0 × 1000 = 1.000; starved to 600 it draws 0.600; at 150 (`LIT_ON_PM`) 0.150, a dim light with a tiny pool (D.3).
511	
512	### D.2 Hard cone scale
513	
514	The `hard_cone_scale` formula is defined as:
515	
516	`texture_scale = reach_px / edge_radius_texels`, with the lint `|reach_px − edge_radius_texels × texture_scale| ≤ 0.1` base px (its own tolerance, separate from the measured ±1 px edge budget of D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
517	
518	**Variables:**
519	
520	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
521	|---|---|---|---|---|
522	| `reach_px` | int | 168 / 288 / 336 / 384 (rows 4 / 1 / 3 / 2 and 8) | `light_shape` REG:121 via the read view (`EM-8`) | the simulation's fade-out radius; for HARD rows it is also the drawn edge; never restated |
523	| `edge_radius_texels` | float | narrow, split, beacon (squares): pass B 2048, pass A 1024; wide (tight box): 1938 (B) / 967 (A); fan (tight box): 1119 (B) / 558 (A) | the texture's measured sidecar (LO-15), produced by a build tool from the imported image | texel distance from the apex to the hard edge along the axis (the square: apex at the midpoint of one edge, so the reach spans the full side; the tight box: LO-15's table) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
524	| `texture_scale` | float | 0.1486..0.375 | output | written to the light |

877	## Edge Cases
878	
879	Each case states the exact outcome and the rule it protects; `LO-n` and `D.n` point at the owner of the behaviour and are not restated. Every case holds at every rung `k_z` in [1, `k_base` + 2] (`k_base` = `k_auto` unless a manual k below Auto is set) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* and under both render passes unless it says otherwise.
880	
881	### Zoom ladder, render passes and the active set
882	
883	- **If the view is 1080p pass A at `k_z` 1 (ρ exactly 9.00)**: the tier is T2, 16 non-shadow lights and 6 lanterns, 2,073,600 lit px; the inclusive boundary is T2, not T3 (D.12). The caps bind only if more than 16 non-shadow lights are in view; truth rules are unchanged.
884	- **If a ladder cut changes `k_z`**: the active set, LOD tier, occluder reach set and slot dwell timers are re-evaluated in one callback; a bound light rebinds only if it left the active set; no light value changes (all lengths are in base px, LO-16) and `state_hash` is identical at every rung (EM-30, AC-86).
885	- **If the target is 2160p at `k_z` 1 (field scale `s` 6.0, outside `PIPE D.5`'s printed 0.6-4.0)**: the tier is T3 (ρ 36.00, caps 12 and 4); the printed range is a stale Pipeline wording (C row 5), not a limit on the ladder.
886	- **If a light's reach disc crosses the field edge**: it is active iff `dx² + dy² ≤ reach_px²`, with `dx = max(0, field_x0 − M − ox, ox − (field_x1 + M))` (likewise `dy`) and `M = VIEW_MARGIN_PX` 24; a 144 px fixture 36 px beyond the margin is active (1,296 ≤ 20,736), one 236 px beyond is not. Integer-only, so the set is reproducible.
887	- **If the narrow cone or beacon magnifies under pass B (1440p `k_z` 6, 2160p `k_z` 6-8)**: the rim softens to 2.25-3.0 screen px but the edge position is the band's half-step and does not move, so the ±1 px lint holds; accepted by ART 8.3 (D.9, D.11).
888	- **If the engine samples light textures from an atlas without mipmaps `[UNV]`**: pass B minification (5.33x narrow, 6.73x wide at `k_z` 1) shimmers as a beam rotates; fallbacks in order: a second lower-density texture swapped for `k_z` ≤ 2 on the existing cut, then accept pass A (spike step 2b).
889	- **If the window, pass or driver changes at run time**: the tier is re-evaluated on that frame as a one-frame cut, a full reconcile runs and every light is a first observation (no warm-up, no governor history); a hidden or minimised window skips the apply step and resumes the same way.
890	
891	### Hard cones and soft pools
892	
893	- **If a beam's `output_pm` is below 600**: its hard rim falls below `LIT_ON_PM` and the rendered rim step shrinks (`EM D.7`); the edge stays at `reach_px` ±1 px. Supported generically, not an MVP case (Suit rules out charge dimming, SE-8).
894	- **If a fixture's `output_pm` is at or below `LIT_ON_PM` (`r_lit` 0)**: it is drawn at `max(r_off, POOL_RESIDUAL_PX)` (20 px at 140 permille, 8 px at 121 and below for R 144) with energy 0.001 × `output_pm`, because a subject already lit there still holds its prompt out to `r_off` (LO-7); the Debug Overlay reports `r_lit` and `r_off`; at the inner ring the 8 px residual pool may sit within 1-2 codes of the floor and vanish, which is acceptable because it is not actionable and the housing still shows the lamp. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
895	- **If a lamp is warming up**: the pool is at its full `r_draw` from the first committed frame while energy ramps over `LAMP_WARM_FRAMES`; `lit` may already be true while the picture is at 40 % on frame 2, bounded by 5 frames (D.14).
896	- **If two soft skirts sum to `lit` in the simulation where the render shows near-black**: accepted as bounded and rare; Emitter State clamping SOFT contributions beyond `r_lit` is an optional refresh, routed only if spike step 2 shows it (LO-7).
897	- **If a tell dip (`M2` 700) is active on a mid plane**: the perceived pool edge moves inward (about 11 px for a 30 % dip, ESTIMATE) while `r_off`, `r_lit` and the prompt do not; AC-56 is evaluated at `m_mod` 1000 and the shrink is an honest dimming. On dark Graphite floors that still-frame difference between a dip and a sag is therefore not reliable, and the cue that holds is the temporal shape, transient versus steady (Named rule 1; Open Question 19).
898	- **If a glowstick wanes**: each integer `reach_px` step redraws the pool at the new `r_draw` on the committed tick, with no tween and no flicker (96 → 24 px reach, `r_off` 84 → 21); waning is simulation state, not a presentation effect (LO-27).
899	- **If the beacon sweeps past a fixed observer**: the governor counts about 0.47 flashes per second (ESTIMATE) and never delays its rotation; the drawn cone leads the committed cone by at most 32 units (2.8°) inside a tick and `lit` uses the committed cone only (LO-27).
900	
901	### Shadow slots, occluders and the shadow origin
902	
903	- **If two non-glowstick deployables are in view (VS-A)**: the nearer by integer `d2` (ties by lower id) holds slot 6 after `SLOT_DWELL_FRAMES`; the other is a non-shadow pool (D.4).
904	- **If a glowstick is the only candidate and the cryo lamp is also in view**: the lamp (rank 1) holds slot 6 and the glowstick is a non-shadow pool; a glowstick holds the slot only when no rank 0 or 1 candidate is in view.
905	- **If two equidistant candidates swap rank every tick**: no swap occurs, because the dwell counter resets each time the challenger loses rank; the incumbent keeps the slot.
906	- **If a slot swap would pop on screen and no pop-free mechanism exists `[UNV]`**: the swap defers up to four dwell periods (120 ticks), then the challenger is demoted to a non-shadow pool and the holder stays (S.2, spike step 3b).
907	- **If the player stands 10-34 px south of a wall**: outcome B shadows start at the foot like the simulation's segment; outcome A puts the node at the chest, which can lie inside the wall footprint, where the engine's behaviour for a light inside a closed occluder is `[UNV]` (an all-around shadow or none); AC-57 records the band (LO-10).
908	- **If Layout bumps `version(section_id)` for a section a shadow light's reach disc intersects**: the polygons are rebuilt and written in the same render callback, in one apply step; a frame is drawn only after the callback returns, so no frame is missing a wall and none lets light through, with no double-buffered set (LO-11) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
909	- **If the bump is for a section wholly outside every reach disc**: it is rebuilt within `OCCLUDER_SYNC_BUDGET_US`, nearest first; its pooled objects are hidden, not freed.
910	- **If a door leaf is half open (`area` between 0 and `area_max`)**: the occluder is the committed leaf rectangle of that tick, `leaf_w = width_px − ⌊width_px × area / area_max⌋` (LY-9), one rectangle with no threshold; the shadow can lead or lag the sprite by at most one tick of leaf travel, accepted because `lit` uses the same rectangle.
911	- **If the shadow-reach set holds more than `OCCLUDER_POLYS_VIEW_MAX` polygons**: every wall is still built, because a missing wall is a P1 lie, and `diag.occluder_overflow` fires as an authoring and budget defect; the cap is a lint and spike target, not a runtime drop.
912	- **If a horror or a crewmate stands in a beam**: it casts no shadow and occludes nothing; actors never occlude (ART 3.2, EM-20).

921	### Budget, demotion and cross-body light
922	
923	- **If more than the tier cap of non-shadow lights are in view**: `cut_order` demotes the lowest to stand-ins with `CUT_FADE_FRAMES` fades (D.19); none is dropped and the simulation is never told; a demoted light draws its stand-in disc to `r_draw` (the 8 px residual when `r_off` is 0), the same edge its pool had (LO-23). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
924	- **If more than the lantern cap of lanterns are in view**: lanterns are a subset of the non-shadow lights and the lowest-priority ones (60) are demoted first, even when the non-shadow total is under its cap.
925	- **If the local seat stands inside the drawn pools of more lights than the tier cap leaves room for (seat protection; design review)**: every light whose drawn pool contains the seat stays bound with full shading, at most `LIGHTS_PER_ITEM_MAX` 12 beyond the cap, counted by `diag.cap_exceeded_by_protected`; lights farther from the seat are demoted first (LO-23). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
926	- **If a demoted lantern is read at the zoom-out (design review)**: its stand-in disc ends at the same `r_draw` as its pool (115 px for a fixture at 600 permille), so counting lanterns at `k_z` 1 and walking up to read a prompt agree to 1 base px on every azimuth, including beside a wall (AC-LO-73; the LO-33 clamp is withdrawn). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)*
927	- **If protected lights fill most of a tier cap (T3 cap 12 with the maximum 10 young fault glows in view)**: the two remaining places go to the highest-priority unprotected lights and every other one is demoted; the floor rule `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` + 2 = 12 is what keeps protected lights from exceeding the cap, and `diag.cap_exceeded_by_protected` counts any excess a later cap change would allow (LO-17, LO-23).
928	- **If a fifth glowing fault shares a view under `TRAIL_LIGHT_REQUESTS_MAX` 4**: it is still rendered and is demoted only once older than 600 ticks; the authoring lint flags any compartment where more than 4 can share a view; dropping a trail light never drops a stamp (LO-23).
929	- **If a bound light drops below the cut line and returns within `CUT_HYSTERESIS_FRAMES` (30 committed ticks)**: it is not rebound, so a pool node cannot ping-pong at the boundary.
930	- **If more than `LIGHTS_PER_ITEM_MAX` (12) lights overlap one tile chunk**: the authoring lint fails; at run time a defect report fires at 14 (`diag.max_item_overlap`); at the engine's 16 `[UNV]` a sim-lit pool would silently vanish over part of the floor, which the 17-light criterion exists to catch.
931	- **If a demotion stand-in sits beside a decoy**: the stand-in is in its own hue with no violet; the decoy keeps its violet rim on top; both are below 0.9 `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`, and they are told apart by rim colour.
932	- **If a light belongs to another live body in view**: it is bound, counted against the caps and lights only its own body's items by its mask bit; bodies beyond `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` 4 draw their lights as OTHER_BODY stand-ins outside the budget; a foreign body bit on a light is a lint failure (LO-24).
933	- **If `MAX_EMITTERS` (96) are all in view**: the stand-in pool is sized `MAX_EMITTERS` − `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` = 90 so that every tier, including T3's cap of 12, can demote the rest (orchestrator ruling: the specialist's 66 would run out at T3).

935	### Modifiers, decoys, channels and hallucination
936	
937	- **If a tell dip and a gutter or warm-up overlap on one fixture**: the factors multiply (`m_mod × env_warm`), the floor excludes the envelope, and the governor counts both transitions (D.13).
938	- **If an Attention tell (L2) and a Horror disturbance (L3) are both active on one fixture**: L3 replaces L2 for that light and a single bounded dip is drawn, then governed (LO-18 iv).
939	- **If an Attention tell tier is active while the cryo-bay lamp (`subkind` EMERGENCY) is in view**: the lamp ignores it (`M2` = `M3` = 1000) and keeps only its baseline gutter at 600-1200 frames, so a dip seen there is always the baseline; the tell shows on every other fixture and lantern, and Attention's non-light world channels carry any tell in the cryo bay (LO-20).
940	- **If a lamp housing's emissive sprite is drawn off while its light is on (false system state, the MVP class)**: the housing is dark and the pool is present; the lie leaks as a pool over an unlit housing; the sprite and the light share no sampler or value path (LO-14).
941	- **If a housing is drawn on while the lamp is dead (`served_pm` 0)**: there is no pool, and no decoy or housing ever adds one; the lie leaks as a missing pool.
942	- **If a `GLOW_EXTENSION` decoy (VS-A) is drawn at the true cone edge**: it is an overlay past the edge with a violet rim; the real hard edge stays at `reach_px` ±1 px and no real `Light2D` member changes (LO-21).
943	- **If the Filter's list holds more than `DECOY_OVERLAYS_MAX` entries**: the earliest 4 are drawn and the rest counted in `diag.decoy_overflow` (D.17).
944	- **If the Perception Filter or the tool layer writes a `Light2D` member**: the source lint fails; there is no run-time guard because a guard would add a check to every write.
945	- **If the Filter's container pass drifts warm over beam pixels (CD-2)**: that is a Filter-side defect; Lighting never tints a real light and the beam stays `#FFE2A8`; the Filter must exclude beam pixels (C row 22).
946	- **If a crewmate is hallucinated as a horror (class 3)**: the Filter may substitute the body but never the beam; the beam's shape and colour are the loadout's and no modifier, decoy or LOD touches them (PC :216, LO-28).
947	- **If Suit's breath-vapour, fog or rime overlays cover a lit area**: they are unlit-layer sprites; no `Light2D` member and no drawn edge changes, so the revealed radius is unchanged (Suit :467).
948	- **If an unknown `hue_class` token arrives**: the light draws Tungsten `#FFCC66` and raises a DIAGNOSTIC; never a sanity-palette hex.
949	- **If the player kills every fixture to go dark**: the HOME ambient slews from 100 to 20 permille in 27 frames (3 permille per frame, D.6), the lit area falls to what runs, and the running loops stay visible as lanterns; there is no penalty and no screen effect (LO-31).
950	- **If the player stacks glowsticks (`GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` 4, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8) over a Coolant Ice mark**: the summed light can exceed the D.8 bound and bloom the stamp; recorded as a residual risk, bounded by the stack cap and by demotion; no rule is changed to hide it.
951	
952	### Governor and accessibility
953	
954	- **If the governor would have to delay a simulation-committed switch, the beacon's aim or a FAULT_GLOW onset**: that is a defect logged as a DIAGNOSTIC and failed by the rapid-toggle stub; the 12-commit-tick spacing that Emitter State's `validate()` enforces (Ask E-E) is what keeps it from arising. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
955	- **If the governor delays a gutter dip to keep a region at or under 3**: the dip starts later, never deeper and never shorter than its 0.3-0.5 s envelope (D.18).
956	- **If the beacon, power arcs and a flare share one region**: the region ring counts the sum, the newer light (higher id) is delayed first, and the beacon rotation and arc onsets pass untouched, so only the flare's dips are retimed.
957	- **If `reduce_flashing` is on (it is the first-launch default: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D79 / X10) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)***: deployables are steady, arcs are a held glow at their mean luminance, the beacon keeps its sweep (sound is Audio's concern; no HUD glyph, ART:741), the cryo gutter and the tell gutter are kept; toggling mid-dip snaps the deployable flicker's `M1` to 1000 on the next frame as one counted transition and leaves the EMERGENCY lamp's `M1` gutter alone. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)*
958	- **If HR-15 is at step 3**: the hull floor rises by 3 codes (D.7) and nothing else changes; web, horrors, filaments, lights and the HUD are untouched; it applies at the next apply step.
959	- **If `CanvasModulate` is found to multiply unshaded items**: carrier B (the default) already avoids it; carrier A stays valid only while one section's ambient applies to the whole view, and is rejected whenever the home ship and a docked derelict can share a view (3 % against 10 %).
960	
961	### Time, restore and holds
962	
963	- **If a light is first observed after boot, a restore, a hold exit, a camera cut or a body re-bind**: it enters STEADY at its L0 value with no warm-up, no fade and no governor history (LO-3); warm-up fires only on an observed 0 to non-zero `output_pm` between two committed ticks.
964	- **If a restore completes (death handling is restart from the last autosave)**: nothing was persisted; every light and occluder is re-derived after Layout's `post_restore` (door leaves are valid only after it, LY-26 c), `version` has reset to 1 so the rebuild is unconditional, and governor windows, dwell timers, gutter epochs, caches and bindings are discarded; the beacon aim jumps to the restored `T` under the hold quad.
965	- **If `LOADING` or `TRANSIT_HOLD` is active**: the world is under the hold quad and lights are not updated; each shader is drawn once with its worst-case light combination so none compiles on first use; the exit is a first observation.
966	- **If the kernel is `PAUSED`**: `present_time` and the kernel clock hold, so envelopes, gutters, the governor window and flare phase freeze and the beacon's drawn aim holds (`tick_alpha` clamped at 1). At 30 fps, if two ticks commit within one render frame, only the final committed state is observed, a 0 → 1000 → 0 pulse inside the burst is never drawn, and the warm-up still takes 83.3 ms because it advances by `present_time`.
967	- **If the read view's `tick` has not advanced**: per-tick work is skipped and per-frame work still runs; **if** more than `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` (256) keys arrive, the `ALL` collapse triggers a full reconcile whose result must equal the incremental one (debug assertion).
968	- **If a body unloads (a derelict undocks, a restore)**: every pooled light, occluder and stand-in bound to it is unbound in one pass and the node count returns to baseline (leak audit).
969	- **If the Presenter's rotation write lands after Lighting's `offset` write within a frame (an ordering defect)**: the apex is off by `|v| × sin(Δθ)`, 12 px for a 20°-per-frame stub, and the apex-equals-chest lint (0.01 px) fails; the ordering is tested with that stub (LO-2).
970	- **If two clients show the same lamp (co-op, later)**: gutter phase may differ because the hash is presentation-only, accepted since the tell tier and not the phase is the information; a remote beam's shape and colour come from the replicated loadout and are never rewritten, and a stale remote record pair holds the last pose without extrapolation (provisional, replication undesigned).

1149	## Game Feel
1150	
1151	The player feels three things of this system, each a measurement before a mood. **The edge is a place you can walk to.** A beam ends where a prompt stops appearing, to ±1 px at every zoom rung; this is the key feel property and it is pass/fail (AC-LO-6 to AC-LO-8); for a pool it is the same edge in both directions (the prompt appears `band_px` inside it on approach and persists exactly to it when leaving) and the same edge when the lamp is a stand-in at the zoom-out (AC-LO-73). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **A lamp catches; it does not lag.** The pool is at its final size from the first committed frame and only its brightness climbs over `LAMP_WARM_FRAMES` (83.3 ms), so a switch reads as a ship's lamp warming, never as input delay (LO-19). **A dip dims; a sag shrinks.** A tell gutter returns to full with the readable radius unchanged and reads as presence; a starvation sag is steady and the pool gets smaller and reads as power (LO-20). The honest qualification (CD-GDD-ALIGN revision): the readable radius is unchanged in a dip, but the perceived edge may move inward on dark floors (about 11 px at a 30 % dip, ESTIMATE), so a still frame is not a reliable way to tell the two apart there, and the redundant cue is the temporal shape, transient versus steady. **The pool ends at the wall.** A non-shadow pool never lights a room the simulation calls dark (LO-33), so what the player sees lit is what the game acts on; under the shipping mechanism this holds for the shadow-casting lights, which include the three nearest wall-near lights (C0), and for the rest within the numeric residual bounds of LO-33 (PD-1, PD-1b). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Shadows never pop: a slot swap crossfades over `SHADOW_FADE_FRAMES` and waits `SLOT_DWELL_FRAMES`.
1152	
1153	**Owners.** Beam-follow and aim feel belong to Player Controller & Input, zoom-step feel to the Render Pipeline; Lighting owns the lamp, edge, shadow and gutter feel above. Feel is checked by capture and playtest (AC-LO-30, AC-LO-58; CD-R1), not automated.
1154	
1155	## UI Requirements
1156	
1157	2D Lighting & Occlusion has no UI of its own. Its only gameplay surface is the lit picture, and what the picture gates by proxy (a prompt, an inspect card) is gated by `lit(ref)` in the HUD and Instruments, never by the renderer (PIPE PR-3; LO-1). Surfaces owned elsewhere:

1160	|---|---|---|---|
1161	| Interaction prompts, inspect cards | HUD, root viewport | on `lit(ref)` change | HUD / Instruments (designed); shown only while `lit` |
1162	| `reduce_flashing`, HR-15 step 0..3 | Settings, per client | on change | Settings / Accessibility (designed: Chart Table & Menus Display & Comfort page; the HR-15 step has no MVP page); Lighting is the consumer (LO-26) |
1163	| First-launch "barely visible" swatch | first-run screen | once | Pipeline (PIPE Open Question 5); drawn with the real floor values, writes no game value |
1164	| Occluder outlines, slot assignment, modifier stack, governor log, `r_lit` circles, LOD tier | Debug Overlay | per frame | `DIAGNOSTIC`, dev builds only, absent from release |
1165	
1166	**Forbidden, stated once:** no light meter, exposure ring, brightness readout, world-space light marker, vignette, fog mask, darkness debuff, or gamma or brightness slider (LO-31; P3 "never a meter").

If the spill does count toward the cap, that would force three lanterns to be demoted whenever the beam is active, which is a concrete, testable discrepancy worth flagging as still unresolved.

I also want to flag AC-LO-53's ambiguity between the Lighting CPU counter budget (1000 µs at P99) and the separate claim that the overall frame P99 must be at most 90% of the frame ceiling -- it's unclear whether that 90% gate applies to the whole frame time or just the Lighting subsystem's counter, especially since the budget stays fixed at 1000 µs while frame ceilings vary by refresh rate (16.6ms vs 33.3ms).

I'm also noting that 1440p and 2160p targets have no assigned reference machine, since R12 only defines RM-DESKTOP at 1920x1080 and RM-DECK for Deck targets -- this leaves the higher-resolution measurement points unassigned, which I should flag as a finding. Then I start checking AC-LO-54's VRAM math for 1080p against the expected byte calculation.

Registry cross-references check out fine too. Now checking LO-33's reference to R_DRAW_MAX_PX against the registry definition for consistency.

Working through the math: if a one-cell wall is 24px thick, then spill beyond the far side equals r_draw − d − 24, which with r_draw at 19 always yields zero or negative, meaning spill can never cross a full-thickness wall. This seems to conflict with LO-35's claim that at d=0 spill can reach 24px — that formula appears to ignore wall thickness entirely and uses R=24 instead of the actual drawn radius of 19, so I need to figure out whether "beyond the wall" in LO-35 actually means something different, like spill into the wall's near face rather than past its far side.

content.content: **The DOCK_STATUS glow (X2, user ruling)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The docked pod's dock-room status glow is self-powered and switched by SYSTEM only (Emitter EM-3), so it belongs to everything the player cannot switch off whenever the pod is berthed (always, except mid-leg). `g_dock = floor(output_pm_D × reach_px_D / 1000)` is its Emitter term; the Emitter and Derelict Authoring own the knobs and have published no value yet, so `g_dock` is `[PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike]` and the shipped rows above are evaluated at `g_dock` 0 until it is published, when the lint adds it. The constraint it must satisfy is that F-15 still holds at every shipped row with the two wake glows: at most 99 runs. Integer model (entry at `L_CEIL`, `r_dark` = 366 + `g_dock`): `g_dock` 0 gives 93 / 96 / 98 runs at rings 1 / 2 / 3; 6 to 24 gives 93 to 94 / 96 to 97 / 99; 30 gives 94 / 97 / 100, so the ring-3 test row fails at 30 (each +1 mAU per tick adds 1.8 AU to `x_dark`, and the ring-3 slack was 6 ticks). The budget handed to Emitter and Authoring is therefore `g_dock ≤ DOCK_GLOW_TERM_MAX` = 24 mAU per tick (for example output 300 × reach 80); at 24 the rows are 94 / 97 / 99 runs (slack 30 / 12 / 0 ticks), the `x_dark_home_lit` ring-1 row is 116 runs against a limit of 119 (slack 18 ticks), and `walk_beam_pm` rises by about 8 permille (F-24, inside its margin). The glow also lifts the lit-idle steady state by `g_dock × 1800` mAU (43 AU at 24), which is why the home-idle figures of F-25 are quoted without it. It is never a tell carrier (AT-20).

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-LO-14, AC-LO-45, AC-LO-23, AC-LO-59, AC-LO-36, AC-LO-50

findings.fix: AC-LO-14: 'across a captured swap, the shadow-region mean changes by at most 1.5 x (full step / SHADOW_FADE_FRAMES) codes per frame and never by more than the full step in one frame'. AC-LO-45: 'over a 360 degree rotation at 1080p k_z 1 pass B, the edge-position std-dev at 8 azimuths is at most 0.25 base px and no rim pixel changes by more than 2 codes between consecutive 1-degree steps'. AC-LO-23: 'regional-mean blue code of Graphite mid: home about 14 +-1 (100 permille), ring-1 derelict about 4 +-1, home at least 2x derelict'. AC-LO-59: 'the scrubber pipe pixels have hue within +-10 degrees of #3FD6E8 and luminance above the floor + 8 codes; lamps off give a lit-area mask equal to the union of running-emitter r_off discs +-1 px'. AC-LO-36: 'edge position with and without the overlay differs by at most 1 base px at 8 azimuths'. AC-LO-50: 'first-draw hitch per variant at most 1.7 ms on RM-DESKTOP and 3.3 ms on RM-DECK, or the variant is pre-warmed'.
